title: `==` is the only equality operator, and comparing two disjoint types does not compile
scope:
the spelling of equality and inequality; what equality *means* for every Novis type, including
the three PHP compares two ways (strings, arrays, objects); what happens when the two operands' static
types cannot both hold the same value; what a `mixed` or union operand does at runtime; and the
comparison `switch` and `match` arms perform. Not in scope: ordering `< <= > >= <=>`, which
[0013](0013.md) owns and this ADR does not touch; truthiness, which
[0035](0035.md) owns; converting between types, which is `as`
([0034](0034.md), [0066](0066.md)); and the
natural ordering `Arr::sort`/`Math::min` use, which `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ordering.rs` owns.

summary.headline: `==` is the only equality operator, and unrelated types cannot be compared
summary.body:
Novis has `==` and `!=`, and nothing else: `===` and `!==` do not parse. `==` never converts
either side, and both sides must have types that can hold the same value — `"1" == 1` stops the
build rather than answering true or false. Where PHP's operators disagreed, the strict answer
wins: two strings compare as text, so `"1" == "01"` is false; objects compare by identity, and
content comparison is a named method. An operand typed `mixed` is decided at run time, and there
a mismatch answers false.
